newsitem.title: USA: Court delays execution of Evinrude heiress killer.
newsitem.headline: Court delays execution of Evinrude heiress killer.

text.p: The Florida Supreme Court Tuesday postponed the execution of one of four men convicted for the 1982 abduction and murder of Evinrude heiress Frances Julia Slater.

John Earl Bush, 38, was scheduled to die in the electric chair Thursday at Florida State Prison near Starke. Attorneys representing him appealed to the Florida high court, which denied the appeal but ordered a stay of the execution until Monday morning to allow federal appeals to proceed.
Following the ruling, the execution was rescheduled for Monday at 7 p.m., the Florida governor's office said.

Bush was one of three men sentenced to death for the April 27, 1982 robbery and murder of Slater, 18, the granddaughter of Ralph Evinrude, who founded the outboard boat motor company Evinrude Motors Co. A fourth accomplice, asleep during most of the crime, is serving a life sentence.

Slater was working as a clerk at Lil' Saints, a convenience store in Stuart, Fla., when Bush, J.B. "Pig" Parker, Alphonso Cave and Terry Wayne Johnson entered the store to rob it. They stole $134 and abducted Slater.

About 12 miles from the robbery scene, Bush stabbed Slater in the stomach and Parker shot her in the back of the head and left her in a ditch, authorities said. Bush was convicted Nov. 18, 1982 and sentenced to death four days later.
This is the third death warrant for Bush, who twice faced a date with the electric chair only to have it postponed. The death warrant expires Oct. 23.
Parker, the trigger man, also is on death row. Cave was originally sentenced to death but the sentence was overturned and he was awaiting resentencing next month.
Cave's attorneys had requested that Bush's execution be postponed so that he could testify in Cave's resentencing hearing. The high court Tuesday denied that request.
